subject: Request: progressive failover + short-term pin for US rollout (telemetry gating)
messages:
From: Tim Saunders <tim.saunders@medicrest.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
Cc: Nicole Park <nicole.park@medicrest.com>
Date: Mon, 29 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Strange latency spikes during our phased rollout (context + ask)

Evelyn —

We started the first wave of our US phased rollout this morning and are seeing intermittent 95th percentile latency spikes that correlate to longer user sessions. The product team is getting customer tickets; the impact is modest so far (~2% of requests), but it's hitting our internal SLA alerting and the legal/compliance folks asked us to request a short-term mitigation while we investigate.

Concretely, we want to request: 1) a temporary pin to the prior model variant for the remainder of wave 1 (48 hours max); and 2) an automated failover rule so that if 95p > 800ms for two consecutive 10-minute windows, traffic shifts back to the pinned variant.

We appreciate Redwood's speed on this — please let us know what approvals you need and whether this triggers an SLA exception.

Thanks,
Tim
——
Tim Saunders
Head of Platform Eng, MediCrest Health
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
To: Tim Saunders <tim.saunders@medicrest.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 29 Mar 2027 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Strange latency spikes during our phased rollout (context + ask)

Tim —

Thanks for the heads-up and the clear ask. We can support a short, controlled pin + an automated telemetry-gated failover. High-level plan below:

- Temporary pin: lock MediCrest wave-1 to model-v2.1 for up to 48 hours; pin will auto-expire unless explicitly extended.
- Telemetry gating: enforce a policy that monitors 95p latency over rolling 10m windows. If 95p > 800ms for two consecutive windows, trigger an immediate failover to the pinned variant and open an incident.
- Observability: we'll surface a per-route trigger in Console, and push a PagerDuty alert to your on-call.
- Risk controls: the failover path is read-only (no config drift) and we will throttle the failover to avoid cascade effects across regions.

Rishi and Laura — tagging you to confirm the automation details and confirm whether this needs an SLA carveout sign-off from Legal/RevOps. Assuming quick thumbs-up, we can enact the pin+failover within 90 minutes. I'll attach the runbook for your review.

Evelyn

--
Evelyn Hart
Senior Manager, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Tim Saunders <tim.saunders@medicrest.com>
Date: Mon, 29 Mar 2027 11:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Strange latency spikes during our phased rollout (context + ask)

Evelyn / Laura —

We can implement the telemetry-gated failover exactly as described. A few engineering notes and constraints:

- Thresholds: 95p threshold = 800ms is reasonable for MediCrest's live traffic profile. We recommend also watching 99p and error rate trends for correlated failures.
- Propagation: the failover is executed by the routing layer; it takes ~20–60s to be fully effective depending on active KV caches. We'll include a cache-warm step to reduce user-impact on the target variant.
- Auto-unpin: pin will auto-expire after 48h. If you want to extend, we need a signed approval from MediCrest PO and a recorded SLA exception (Legal).
- Safety net: if error rate increases > 1% within 30m after failover, we'll auto-revert and create a high-priority incident.

I've attached the deploy_failover_playbook.pdf and a quick thresholds spreadsheet (telemetry_gate_thresholds.xlsx). Ready to flip the switch once Legal signs the exception.

-rishi

--
Rishi Malhotra
Engineering Lead, Runtime & Serving
Redwood Inference
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 29 Mar 2027 13:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Strange latency spikes during our phased rollout (context + ask)

Evelyn / Rishi —

Good plan. Two operational asks from Product/RevOps before we authorize the SLA exception:

1) Documented acceptance criteria for success post-failover (we'll want low user impact and no data-loss scenarios).
2) A short-term credit proposal for MediCrest should the failover lead to measurable degradation in throughput or error budget consumption.

If Tim can confirm (1) and (2) is acceptable, I will route an internal SLA exception approval to Legal and RevOps. We should keep the pin duration to 48 hours unless absolutely necessary.

-L

--
Laura Bennett
Director, Product Management
Redwood Inference
From: Tim Saunders <tim.saunders@medicrest.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 30 Mar 2027 15:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Strange latency spikes during our phased rollout (context + ask)

Evelyn / Laura / Rishi —

Thanks for the quick coordination. Quick responses to your asks:

1) Acceptance criteria: after failover we expect 95p <= 650ms within 15 minutes and no more than 0.5% error rate increase over baseline in the subsequent 60 minutes. If those are met we'll continue the rollout.
2) Credit proposal: MediCrest accepts a one-time 15% service credit on the proportion of traffic in wave 1 should we see error-rate > 1% or customer-facing incidents attributable to the failover.

Please proceed with the pin + telemetry-gated failover. We'll sign any required SLA exception paperwork; Nicole will follow up with Legal.

—
Tim
